description: A waveshaper that reads a two-dimensional surface: two input signals are the X and Y coordinates, and the height of the surface at that point is the output

params.text: Shapes the surface itself, blending the X and Y terrains together by whatever function the map button has chosen
Offsets where the X input reads on the surface, -1 to +1
Offsets where the Y input reads on the surface, -1 to +1
Sets one of the two voltages the main scan output runs between, -5V to +5V; patching the A input takes this knob out of circuit
Multiplies the B input by -1 to +1 to set the other voltage the main scan output runs between; with nothing patched to B the input reads 5V, so the knob alone gives -5V to +5V
Attenuates the X signal input, from nothing at fully counter-clockwise to all of it at fully clockwise
Attenuates the Y signal input, from nothing at fully counter-clockwise to all of it at fully clockwise
Steps through what a pulse at the Jump input does: Reverse, which turns the scan round, or Teleport, which jumps it elsewhere
Steps forward through the eight Y terrains: Slopes, Hills, Pyhisics World, Shapeshifting Range, Multiplier Mountains, Synthville, Steppes and Blockland
Steps through the function that combines the X and Y terrains into one surface: Add, Multiply, Difference or Lighten
Steps backward through the eight X terrains, wrapping round at the start
Steps backward through the eight Y terrains, wrapping round at the start
Steps forward through the eight X terrains: Slopes, Hills, Pyhisics World, Shapeshifting Range, Multiplier Mountains, Synthville, Steppes and Blockland
Nothing in the Rack module reads this button; on the hardware it opens the preset menu

inputs.text: One of the two voltages the main scan output runs between; patched here, it overrides the A knob
The other voltage the main scan output runs between, multiplied by the B knob; unpatched it reads 5V
Modulates the surface shape, at 384 units of the internal 12-bit control range per volt
The X coordinate read into the surface, through the X input attenuation knob
The Y coordinate read into the surface, through the Y input attenuation knob
A rising edge here reverses or teleports the scan, according to the JUMP input response button
While this is high the A and B levels are frozen at the values they held

outputs.text: The height of the surface at the scanned point, scaled between the A and B levels
A 5V square taken from one bit of the scan
The height of the surface without the A and B scaling
A 5V square taken from a second bit of the scan

notes: the A input is normalled to the A knob: with nothing patched the knob sets that voltage, and patching a cable into A takes the knob out of circuit entirely.
the B input is normalled to 5V and the B knob multiplies whatever arrives by -1 to +1. Unpatched the knob is a -5V to +5V source; patched it attenuverts the cable.
the main output is the module's own signal scaled between the A and B levels. Set both of those to 0V and the main output is silent whatever else the module is doing.
each of the six buttons steps to the next mode when clicked. Hovering one names the mode and its number; right-click and you can type either to jump straight to it.
the four arrow buttons around the diamond step the X and Y terrains: two of them step Y forward and back, and the other two step X.
menu: Stock presets: Slopes, Physics World, Multiplier Mountains, Synthville, Steppes, Blockland — sets all six buttons at once to a factory combination
Select wavetable set — loads a surface file from disk in place of the one the module ships with
